issues.description: The problem statement / UML and textual instructions require the Animal name accessor methods (getName and setName) to have protected visibility so subclasses can access them while preventing external access. In the reference solution, getName() and setName(...) are implemented as public methods. This visibility mismatch contradicts the explicit guidance in the problem text and UML and may confuse students about the intended encapsulation level.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the visibility of getName() and setName(...) in Animal.java to protected to match the problem statement and UML. Update any code that relies on public access accordingly (subclasses can still call the methods).

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement denotes the Animal constructor as protected (indicated by '# Animal(String): void'), but the reference solution defines the Animal(String) constructor as public. This is a structural visibility inconsistency that could confuse students about the intended instantiation policy for Animal (e.g., whether it should only be constructible by subclasses).
issues.suggestedFix: Adjust the Animal constructor visibility in the solution to protected to align with the UML and problem intent. If the exercise intends Animal to be instantiable only via subclasses, use a protected constructor; otherwise, update the problem text/UML to specify a public constructor.
